concepts.def: Belonging to the prevailing key — no chromatic alteration.
Using notes outside the prevailing key.
Based on a modal scale (e.g. Dorian, Phrygian).
Sustained note (often tonic or dominant) under changing harmony.

walkthroughs.body_html: Diatonic writing remains within the key. Chromatic introduces accidentals for colour or modulation. Modal writing uses scales like Dorian or Mixolydian (Vaughan Williams, jazz).
A pedal sustains under shifting harmonies, creating tension or anchoring. The dominant pedal at the end of a development passage prepares the return of tonic.
Mark playing techniques: pizzicato, con sordino, sul ponticello, col legno (strings); muted, stopped (horn); flutter-tongue (winds). Each colours the texture.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
It has only five notes.
All notes are raised by a semitone.
The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).

mcqs.q: What does modulation mean in music?
options: Adjusting volume electronically.
It has only five notes.
Changing from one key to another within a piece.
Changing tempo or dynamics.

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
